subject.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64

question: Should a configured image-understanding failure permanently become text-only, accepting loss of the current raw-image recovery fallback, or should OpenClaw retain a safe image-recovery design that cannot persist into later session context?
rationale: The branch fixes a real session-state failure, but current main explicitly preserves raw-image fallback recovery and the correct balance between screenshot availability and history safety is a user-visible product contract.

options.title: Adopt text-only recovery
options.body: Approve the branch’s text-only configured-vision failure behavior as the canonical contract because preventing multi-turn session contamination outweighs fallback image inspection.

options.title: Retain safe image recovery
options.body: Ask for a redesigned recovery path that preserves current-turn screenshot usefulness while ensuring image media cannot persist into later tool-result history.

options.title: Pause for browser-owner design
options.body: Hold the PR until an owner defines the supported failure behavior and its compatibility expectations.

recommendation.title: Adopt text-only recovery
recommendation.body: Approve the branch’s text-only configured-vision failure behavior as the canonical contract because preventing multi-turn session contamination outweighs fallback image inspection.

likelyOwner.reason: No concrete browser-area owner could be established from the available current-main provenance.
